item_name: SiamMOT (Shuai et al. CVPR 2021) and works where a single-object tracker proposal enters MOT association cost; TrackTrack (Shim et al. CVPR 2025); MOTIP (Gao et al. CVPR 2025)
depth_level: Full analysis (code, ablations, all fields), as set in the item. Three primary sources read in full text (SiamMOT incl. supplementary tables; TrackTrack CVF open-access version; MOTIP arXiv v2 incl. appendix). A fourth 2023+ candidate (OmniTracker, TPAMI, arXiv 2303.12079, tracker supplies appearance priors to detection) was screened from the abstract only and is not used as evidence [uncertain].

task_and_output: SiamMOT: online MOT of persons; for each active track a Siamese forward tracker (EMM) correlates the track's region features from frame t with a search region (2x target size) in frame t+delta and outputs a dense visibility confidence map v_i and box-corner offset map p_i; the decoded output is a tracked box plus visibility score v_i^{t+delta}. Detections overlapping a tracked box (IoU >= 0.5) are suppressed; the track continues if v_i > alpha (0.4), new tracks are born from unmatched detections with score > beta (0.6). TrackTrack: online tracking-by-detection; output is the matching between Kalman-predicted tracks and an enlarged candidate set (high-confidence after NMS, low-confidence after NMS, high-confidence boxes deleted by NMS), plus a new-track initialization rule; no learned component in the association. MOTIP: online MOT; output is an ID label for every current detection, chosen by K+1-way classification over in-context ID tokens of the past T frames of tracklets plus a special 'newborn' token.
data_and_independent_videos: SiamMOT: ablations on MOT17-train (7 videos), Caltech Roadside Pedestrians (CRP, 7 videos about 20 min each, car-mounted camera) and TAO-person validation (826 videos); models for ablation trained on CrowdHuman images (image training with simulated pairs), i.e. evaluation videos unseen; state of the art on MOT17-test (public detections), TAO-person val, HiEve test (13 videos). TrackTrack: MOT17, MOT20, DanceTrack; ablations on MOT17-val (half-split of train videos, standard convention) and DanceTrack-val; detector YOLOX-x trained on each target dataset plus CrowdHuman/WiderPerson; ReID SBS50 trained per dataset. MOTIP: DanceTrack (100 videos), SportsMOT (240 videos), BFT (birds), MOT17 in appendix; ablations on DanceTrack-val after training on DanceTrack-train (separate videos). None of the three used BDD100K MOT; TAO-person contains some BDD clips (SiamMOT section 4.1).
target_size_and_input_resolution: SiamMOT: Faster-RCNN with DLA-34 + FPN, training images with shorter side 800 px; EMM template features 15x15, search features 30x30 (search region r = 2 times target); target sizes are person boxes (pixel size not reported). TrackTrack: no learned input; YOLOX-x detector at the usual YOLOX MOT resolution (not stated in main text) [uncertain]. MOTIP: Deformable DETR ResNet-50, input shorter/longer side 800/1440, object embedding C = 256. Our setting for comparison: FlyVis eye crop of 721 grey hexals rendered from a crop around the predicted box (eye_size 391 px in the R1 case), target around 9x12 lattice steps.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: SiamMOT: native MOT frame rates (about 30 fps for MOT17), training pairs at most 1 s apart; CRP has strong camera motion; tau (max unseen frames) saturates at 30 frames = 1 s (Table 3). TrackTrack: native MOT17/MOT20/DanceTrack rates, NSA Kalman motion model, lost tracks re-tracked up to 2 s; no camera-motion compensation mentioned in main text. MOTIP: training samples T+1 frames with random intervals, T = 29 (DanceTrack), 59 (SportsMOT), 19 (BFT); SportsMOT has camera motion.
detector_and_exemplar: SiamMOT: joint Faster-RCNN detector; the exemplar is the track's own last region feature (last predicted location and feature during occlusion), i.e. a one-frame template updated every frame. TrackTrack: external YOLOX-x detections; tracks represented by Kalman state, EMA appearance (FastReID), confidence and direction like Hybrid-SORT; no exemplar matching beyond ReID cosine. MOTIP: DETR detector; the 'exemplar' is the whole set of past T object embeddings of each trajectory concatenated with its ID token.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: SiamMOT: everything trained jointly end-to-end: L = l_rpn + l_detect + l_motion; EMM loss = focal loss on the visibility map (positive inside ground-truth next box) + centerness-weighted IoU loss on box offsets; triplets: positive (P), negative (N: region contains no person), hard (H: person present in R_t but not in S_{t+delta}). IMM has about 400x more parameters than EMM (supplement). TrackTrack: no training of the association (training-free); detector and ReID trained separately. MOTIP: DETR + ID decoder (6 layers by default, Table 9) + learnable ID dictionary (K = 50; 200 on MOT17) trained jointly: L = 2.0 focal + 5.0 L1 + 2.0 GIoU + 1.0 cross-entropy ID loss; gradients through DETR only on 4 of the T frames; trajectory augmentation with token-drop (lambda_occ = 0.5) and ID-token swap (lambda_sw = 0.5).

None of the three reports a paired bootstrap or per-video variability.

tested_conditions: SiamMOT: unseen videos yes (ablation models trained on CrowdHuman images, tested on MOT17/CRP/TAO); target absence yes in the sense of visibility score and hard triplets (target not in search region), and keeping invisible tracks up to tau frames; similar distractors partly (hard triplets, claim that pixel-level supervision reduces false matching to distractors - no separate distractor metric); occlusion yes (tau study); night/low light not reported; sequential operation on own predictions yes (online inference, template = last own prediction). TrackTrack: unseen videos yes (val halves / test server); target absence not reported as a separate condition; similar distractors yes indirectly (DanceTrack); occlusion yes (Fig. 5 severity analysis); night/low light not reported; sequential operation yes (online). MOTIP: unseen videos yes (val/test); target absence yes via 'newborn' class and id-threshold (an object not matched to any trajectory); similar distractors yes (DanceTrack, BFT); occlusion yes (trajectory token-drop augmentation, qualitative appendix D.3); night/low light not reported; sequential operation on own predictions yes, and the paper explicitly simulates own ID errors in training by ID-token swap.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanisms. SiamMOT: the single-object tracker's box does not enter a cost matrix as a shift of a motion prior; it replaces association - the tracked box becomes the track's observation, detections overlapping it (IoU >= 0.5) are deleted, and whether the track continues is decided by the Siamese visibility score, not by detection matching. The SOT is trained on positive, negative (no object in the template) and hard (object absent from the search region) triplets so its visibility score can say 'not here'; a cosine window and scale penalty (Eq. 5) discourage large jumps. TrackTrack: association is made from the track's point of view - iterative mutual-minimum pairs (Eq. 2) over one joint cost matrix that includes low-confidence and NMS-deleted boxes with additive penalties tau_p, tau_q (Eq. 1), the threshold tightens each round; new tracks are suppressed by NMS against matched tracks treated as confidence-1 anchors (TAI). The structural lesson for us: an uncertain alternative hypothesis can be added to the candidate set with a penalty instead of replacing the existing one. MOTIP: association is a classification of each detection into one of the live track IDs or 'newborn', trained with cross-entropy on the actual ID decision, with augmentation that simulates occlusion and the tracker's own ID errors. Proposed modification for us (not published): enter the FlyVis centre correction of a lost track as a second, penalised prior hypothesis in the existing ByteTrack cost row (cost = min(cost with Kalman prior, cost with fly-corrected prior + penalty)) and do not overwrite the Kalman mean unless the corrected hypothesis is the one that wins the match. This directly removes the R1 failure mode, where the overwrite turned a correct match (cost 0.1235) into an impossible one (1.0).
transfer_limits: (1) Representation: SiamMOT EMM uses 15x15/30x30 deep RGB region features from a jointly trained detector backbone; FlyVis gives 34 motion/brightness cell types on 721 grey hexals - no evidence that a visibility head of SiamMOT quality is reachable from these features; our own z13 cards show refusal/selection is the weak part (z13_threshold_diagnostic_v1: max share of successful corrections 4.93-13.89% vs required 90%; z13_balanced_ridge_v1: 2 useful of 84 selected). (2) Search area: SiamMOT search region is 2x the target and the gain saturates at tau = 30 frames because objects leave the search region; our eye window is also about 2x the target and lost episodes up to 30 frames at 30 Hz, so the same ceiling applies. (3) Our stand is YOLO26s at 960, conf 0.01 + XYWHByteTrack + MASA; the correction enters before ByteTrack first association by overwriting t.mean[:2] of lost tracks (tracking/z13_ridge_localizer.py before_associate); the cost is fused 1-IoU with score and match threshold 0.8 - a 79.7 px shift on a 60x79 px box gives IoU 0 and therefore an unrecoverable miss. (4) SiamMOT's replacement-style integration assumes the SOT is reliable; with our selection precision far below 90% this integration would amplify harm. (5) TrackTrack/MOTIP were tuned on pedestrian/dancer data at native frame rates; BDD100K MOT ground truth is at 5 fps (every 6th frame at 30 Hz), so loss-on-decision training like MOTIP has only sparse ID supervision. (6) Project zoo numbers for TrackTrack/HybridSORT are from an older 640 setup on 50 videos (plan section 3.6, point 9 says re-measurement is required), so they do not transfer to the current stand. (7) Finding the previous target among similar neighbours or refusing: TrackTrack's mutual-minimum rule naturally refuses a track-detection pair when a neighbour track is closer to that detection; this is an association-side refusal that FlyVis does not have to provide.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1 (right object and refusal): design analogy - SiamMOT separates 'target present' (visibility map, trained with hard triplets where the target is absent) from location; MOTIP separates 'existing ID' vs 'newborn' as an explicit class; TrackTrack refuses via mutual-minimum. 5.2 (target model and memory): weak - SiamMOT uses only last-frame template; MOTIP keeps T past embeddings per track. 5.3 (core training through applied readout): design analogy and caution - SiamMOT joint training gives MOTA 63.3 vs 61.5; MOTIP shows loss on the applied ID decision beats ReID/contrastive losses on the same frozen features (55.4 vs 29.4/41.0 HOTA, Table 5) - this is the strongest published support for training through the decision actually applied. 5.4 (benefit for association): direct - the three works show three different entry points (replace observation, extra candidate with penalty, ID classification); together with our R1 case they indicate the entry point, not only the readout quality, decides whether a wrong correction costs HOTA.
candidate_node_change: Node: readout -> state transfer into the tracker (how the fly answer is applied). Change: 'additive hypothesis' application of the FlyVis centre answer: for each lost track keep the Kalman prior box B_k and add a fly-shifted box B_f (same size); association cost for that track row = min(c(B_k, d), c(B_f, d) + pen); the Kalman mean is updated with the fly centre only if the B_f hypothesis is the matched one; otherwise the correction is discarded for this frame. Optionally the fly confidence sets pen (higher confidence -> lower penalty), keeping a fixed penalty as the main variant. Controls (rule 6.16): (1) stand without correction; (2) the same additive-hypothesis rule fed by the no-fly eye-input ridge R1 (and, as a second no-fly control, by a pure Kalman/IoU guard: do not apply any correction when the Kalman prior already has a candidate with cost < 0.8); (3) the same rule fed by stock FlyVis C; (4) modernised centred D. FlyVis contribution only if (4)/(3) > (2). Minimal check (cheap, on saved data, train26 only): replay saved lost-track steps and count how many of the R1/C/D interventions that destroyed a cost < 0.8 match become harmless and how many useful re-captures survive; then the R1 dev case 0355243b-d696291a frame 183 must give track 6 -> detection 2 (diagnostic, not tuning). Stop condition written before the run: if on train26 the additive rule fed by D does not keep at least the same number of correct re-captures as the overwrite rule while removing the harmful ones, or if (4) - (2) on the pre-registered HOTA comparison has a 95% paired-bootstrap interval including 0, stop this application change and record that the gain belongs to the tracker guard, not to FlyVis.
strongest_objection: The additive-hypothesis change is an improvement of how the tracker consumes a signal, i.e. environment engineering by the project's own boundary (AGENTS.md: heads/filters over the fly signal are application, not modernisation). In the R1 case the correct answer was already available from the Kalman prior, so an external guard ('keep the prior if it already matches') reproduces the whole benefit with no FlyVis at all; the published works give no evidence that small motion features can supply the missing benefit (finding the target when the prior fails). It also makes FlyVis gains even smaller: the fly answer would only matter where the prior fails and the fly is right, which our selection data says is rare (2 useful of 84 selected in z13_balanced_ridge_v1).
evidence_strength: SiamMOT: peer-reviewed CVPR 2021, public code, widely cited; ablations single-run without intervals - moderate. TrackTrack: peer-reviewed CVPR 2025, public code (README verified); main ablations single-run, hyper-parameters per dataset in supplement not read; our own zoo reproduced the 'fewest ID switches' property (IDSw 503 vs 4380) on BDD100K at an older setting - moderate. MOTIP: peer-reviewed CVPR 2025 (v2), public code (not opened); strong internal comparisons on frozen features (Table 5) but single runs and only pedestrians/dancers/birds - moderate. Overall for our decision (where the correction enters): moderate as design analogy, weak as direct evidence for FlyVis features.
where_distinction_is_made: SiamMOT: in a separate learned output - the visibility confidence map trained by focal loss with hard triplets (target absent from search region) and negatives (no object in template); a map maximum is accepted only if visibility > alpha = 0.4; jumps are additionally penalised by a cosine window and scale Gaussian (Eq. 5), so a maximum far from the prior is down-weighted before the decision. Similar distractor vs target is not separated explicitly beyond this training. TrackTrack: in the association decision - a track takes a detection only if they are mutual minima across the joint cost matrix and below tau_m (tightening each round), so a detection closer to another track is refused for this one; insufficient data is handled by penalties for low-confidence and NMS-deleted boxes. MOTIP: in the classification decision - K identity classes plus a 'newborn' class, threshold id = 0.2 for accepting an ID, self-attention among current detections to prevent two detections taking the same ID; duplicate IDs resolved by highest confidence. None of the three separates 'target outside search area' from 'target occluded' explicitly; SiamMOT notes the tau gain saturates when objects leave the 2x search region.
feature_dependence: All three depend on rich learned appearance: SiamMOT on DLA-34 RGB region features (joint training adds MOTA 63.3 vs 61.5); MOTIP on DETR object embeddings (C = 256) - and Table 5 shows the decision formulation matters greatly on the same features; TrackTrack uses FastReID cosine in its cost but its two contributions (TPA, TAI) are purely geometric/score-based and training-free, which is why its structure transfers to motion-only signals. No evidence in any of the three that the mechanism works on small temporal motion/brightness features like 34 FlyVis cell types on 721 grey columns [uncertain whether a SiamMOT-like visibility head would work on FlyVis features; untested].
association_consequence: SiamMOT: the SOT box becomes the track observation and suppresses overlapping detections - identity is preserved by construction if the SOT is right and lost (or swapped) if it is wrong; there is no cost fallback. TrackTrack: identity preservation comes from track-perspective mutual-minimum matching and from blocking new tracks near matched tracks (TAI) - this directly targets fragmentation like our R1 case (new ID 155 born next to lost track 6). MOTIP: identity is the decision itself. For our stand: the R1 case shows the overwrite of the Kalman mean turned cost 0.1235 into 1.0 (> 0.8) and produced fragmentation (ID 155 from frame 184). An external guard gives the same effect in this case without the mechanism: (a) 'do not apply a correction if the uncorrected prior already has a candidate below the match threshold', (b) shift limit relative to box size (79.7 px vs box width about 60 px), or (c) additive min-cost hypothesis. Therefore any HOTA gain from changing the entry point must be credited to the tracker unless the fly-fed variant beats the no-fly-fed variant under the identical rule.
difference_from_tried: Tried in the project: overwrite application of centre corrections for lost tracks with confidence gate tau (R1, C, D, centred D; z13_center_hota_v1), utility heads deciding whether to apply (z13_next_utility_v1, z13_map_utility_v1), pairwise targets, ranking of 3 peaks, framewise candidate identity, observation/query memory, boundary peak suppression, absolute confidence, balanced/hinge losses, core training through target model. Not tried: (a) changing the entry point from state overwrite to an additional penalised hypothesis in the cost row (TrackTrack-style candidate set extension), (b) a decision loss on the applied association (MOTIP-style ID / newborn classification) instead of losses on the centre map, (c) SiamMOT-style hard/negative triplets for the visibility decision - partly tried through absent class and negatives in exemplar matching, so (c) is not new. The utility heads were attempts to decide applicability from map/geometry features; the new element here is that applicability is decided by the association cost itself (the correction must win a match), which requires no learned head. Difference is real for (a) and (b); for (c) no meaningful difference.
memory_write_policy: SiamMOT: template = last predicted location and its feature, rewritten every frame, also during occlusion (no check); tracks kept up to tau = 30 frames. TrackTrack: Kalman state and EMA ReID appearance updated after a match (EMA details in supplement, not read); lost tracks re-tracked up to 2 s. MOTIP: stores the past T frames of matched object embeddings per trajectory; written after the ID decision of each frame (own predictions, no extra check); robustness to own wrong writes is trained by ID-swap augmentation (lambda_sw = 0.5).
distractor_representation: SiamMOT: implicit, via hard/negative triplets and pixel-level supervision in the loss. TrackTrack: explicit through the shared cost matrix - neighbouring tracks compete for the same detection (mutual minimum), and matched tracks act as anchors suppressing new tracks. MOTIP: explicit - all live trajectories are classes in the same decision, with self-attention among current detections.
refusal_evidence_horizon: SiamMOT: single frame visibility score, but a track is killed only after tau consecutive low-visibility frames (accumulation for termination, not for acceptance). TrackTrack: single frame, rule-based (threshold and mutual minimum). MOTIP: single frame classification conditioned on up to T past frames of each trajectory (history-conditioned single-frame decision).
loss_on_applied_decision: SiamMOT: no - loss on visibility and box maps of the SOT (an intermediate), though the SOT output is the applied observation; the association rule itself is not trained. TrackTrack: no loss (training-free rules). MOTIP: yes - cross-entropy directly on the ID label that is applied at inference (with a 'newborn' class), with augmentation simulating own errors.
association_entry_point: SiamMOT: track candidates/state update - the SOT box replaces the detection as the track observation, overlapping detections are suppressed, continuation by visibility score. TrackTrack: matching cost (joint cost matrix with penalties per candidate type) and track-creation rule (TAI). MOTIP: the decision itself (ID classification replaces cost matrix and Hungarian). Our stand now: state update before matching (overwrite of the Kalman centre of lost tracks), which then acts on the matching cost; proposed: matching cost as an additional penalised hypothesis, state update only after the hypothesis wins.
no_fly_control_equivalent: (1) Kalman-prior guard: skip the correction whenever the uncorrected prior already has a candidate with fused cost < 0.8 (would have fixed the R1 case alone). (2) Shift limit relative to box size (e.g. reject shifts larger than a fixed fraction of max(w, h), fixed before the run). (3) Additive min-cost hypothesis fed by the eye-input ridge R1 (no FlyVis core). (4) TrackTrack-style Track-Aware Initialization: NMS of unmatched high-score detections against lost/matched tracks to suppress new IDs near a lost track - addresses the fragmentation half of the R1 case. (5) Hybrid-SORT weak cues (confidence, height IoU) in the cost (see N18). The mandatory no-fly control for the proposed change is (3) together with (1): the fly-fed version must beat both.
hard_subset_evaluation: SiamMOT: CRP selected as a fast camera-motion dataset (separate table), no hard subset inside a dataset. TrackTrack: Fig. 5 orders 5 MOT17/MOT20 videos by occlusion severity (ratio of overlaps IoU > 0.6 to overlaps IoU > 0.1) and shows larger gains for more severe occlusion - post-hoc per-video analysis, not a pre-selected subset. MOTIP: DanceTrack as hard dataset (uniform appearance, nonlinear motion); no within-dataset subset.
temporal_information_availability: All three are strictly online: SiamMOT uses frames t and t+1 only (zero latency; 17.6 fps on 720p for EMM); TrackTrack uses current detections and past track state (zero latency); MOTIP uses the current frame and up to T past frames with a causal attention mask (zero latency). The proposed additive-hypothesis application also uses only current and past frames and acts in the same frame. None of the benefits relies on seeing the continuation; note that the R1 analysis itself used later frames (184-191, GT185) only to diagnose, not as an input to the correction.
